interpretation: 2.7-8: 'pepisteumai to euangelion tēs akrobystias kathōs Petros tēs peritomēs, ho gar energēsas Petrō eis apostolēn tēs peritomēs enērgēsen kai emoi eis ta ethnē'; 2.9: 'Iakōbos kai Kēphas kai Iōanēs, hoi dokountes styloi einai, dexias edōkan emoi kai Barnaba koinōnias'. Read as a first-hand report that Peter, identified with the Cephas of 2.9 (the usual reading, not stated in the text), was one of three recognised leaders of the Jerusalem community and held an apostolate to the circumcised. Context read: the whole of chapter 2 (2.11-14: Paul opposes Cephas at Antioch) and 1.13-24 in the pinned NT-GAL-1 (1.18: three years after his call Paul went up 'historēsai Kēphan' and stayed with him fifteen days). Limits: the report is about standing, not its origin; Paul names James first in 2.9 and says that the standing of 'those reputed to be something' makes no difference to him and that they added nothing to him (2.6), so the text does not by itself give Peter a primacy; it does not mention any commission of Jesus. It is relevant to the Peter-directed reports (Matthew 16.18-19, John 21.15-17) only as a datum both the case and its rivals must explain (ATTEMPT-GOVERNING-COMMISSION-ATTESTATION).
